items.headline: Stocks Closed Higher Friday, October 2nd, on Cooling Job Market Data
items.summary: U.S. equities rallied on Friday, October 2, with major indices closing in positive territory, largely driven by a weaker-than-expected September jobs report. This data eased investor concerns about aggressive Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, significantly reducing the probability of an October rate increase. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.2%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5% for the day. For the week, however, the S&P 500 and Dow closed lower, while the Nasdaq posted a modest gain.

items.headline: September Jobs Report Signals Cooling Labor Market
items.summary: The U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September, significantly less than the 84,000-90,000 jobs anticipated by economists. The unemployment rate also ticked up to 4.2% from 4.1%. This slowdown in hiring, alongside revisions that erased 60,000 jobs from prior months, was a primary driver for Friday's market rally, as it reduced expectations for an October Federal Reserve interest rate hike.

items.headline: Odds of October Fed Rate Hike Plummet
items.summary: Following the softer-than-expected September jobs report, the implied probability of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates in October dropped sharply, falling from approximately 70% earlier in the week to between 18% and 22.7% by Friday's close. This reassessment of monetary policy expectations provided a tailwind for the stock market.

items.headline: Technology and Energy Lead Weekly Gains; Healthcare and Financials Lag
items.summary: For the trading week ending October 2, the Technology sector led with a 1.44% gain, followed by Energy, which rose 1.21%. In contrast, Healthcare and Financial Services were the worst-performing sectors, declining by 2.57% and 2.45% respectively. Consumer Discretionary also showed strength on Friday, gaining 1.4%.

items.headline: S&P 500 Q3 Earnings Growth Projected Above 29%
items.summary: As the third-quarter earnings season approaches, the S&P 500 is forecast to report year-over-year earnings growth of 29.5%, marking the third consecutive quarter of growth exceeding 25%. This optimistic outlook is supported by positive revisions to earnings estimates and strong guidance from many companies.

items.headline: Micron Technology Reports Strong Q4 Earnings Beat
items.summary: Micron Technology Inc. ($MU) announced robust fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $33.42 per share, an eleven-fold increase from the previous year and surpassing analyst estimates. Revenue surged 379.3% year-over-year to $54.23 billion, driven by strong pricing and AI-led memory and storage demand.
